summary: Indian Harbour (Paddy's Head) light, St. Margaret's Bay: a square tower put in operation in 1901, one keeper until 1945, restored 2017-2018. Coast Guard owned; tower closed.

structures.note: 1901 report: 33 ft (10 m) to the top of the lantern vent; Coast Guard list today: 9.4 m. Lantern replaced with a new aluminum one, set on 7 Feb 2018.

access.note: Tower closed. LighthouseFriends: grounds and tower closed, and the last part of the approach is over private property. Rowlett: site open, tower closed, reached by a strenuous walk. The two disagree on the grounds.

events.note: Put in operation 20 May 1901 (1901 Marine report)
Erected by the department by day labour under foreman Amos McLennan, cost $728.24
Henry Boutillier appointed first keeper 6 June 1901 at $100 a year (LighthouseFriends)
Barque Ashlow an obstruction in Indian Harbour; removed under contract for $100. The report does not place it near the light.
Four wooden spar buoys placed in April 1904 to mark shoals in the harbour channel
George Richardson hired as caretaker for maintenance and reporting problems
Maintenance taken over by the Department of Transportation
Friends of Paddy's Head Lighthouse formed; sought ownership of the tower to look after it
Vinyl siding on the tower; new aluminum lantern room placed 7 Feb 2018

corrections.why: The 1901 Marine report says the light was put in operation on 20 May 1901. The record has no first-lit year.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1901 report gives 33 ft (10 m) to the top of the lantern vent; the Coast Guard list gives the structure as 9.4 m. The sources do not say how each was measured. Both are kept; the record's 9.4 m is the Coast Guard figure.
The 1901 report gives visibility of 7 miles; the Coast Guard list now gives a range of 9 nautical miles. The 1901 unit is not stated. The record's 9 nm is the current figure.

notes_for_editor: Access conflict to check by a human before publication: LighthouseFriends says grounds and tower closed and access to the lighthouse itself is over private property; Rowlett says site open, tower closed. The story says the tower is closed and warns against crossing private land. Keeper spelling: Boutilier (1901 list, scan 260, read from a name-and-station OCR line, not a column) and Boutillier (LighthouseFriends); the story uses LighthouseFriends' spelling in the prose. R. J. Boutillier, Superintendent of Sable Island in the same 1901 list, is a different man and is not linked. Heights: the 1901 report gives 33 ft (10 m) to the top of the lantern vent; the Coast Guard list gives the structure 9.4 m. Both are stated; the sources do not say how each was measured. Range: the 1901 report gives visibility of 7 miles without a method; the Coast Guard list gives a nominal range of 9 nm. Both are stated. Colour: the 1901 report says the whole building was painted white; the Coast Guard list says white square tower with red upper portion; Rowlett says the lantern is painted red. All three are stated in Today, not settled. Buoys: the 1903 report (Sessional Paper 1904, p. 63, scan 76) already lists four spar buoys in the harbour, without a date; the 1904 report (p. 37, scan 50) dates their establishment to April 1904. The story says the sources do not say whether these are the same buoys. The 1904 report OCR reads 'frona Wreck island'; the story reads it as 'from'. The 1903 Ashlow entry is harbour-level and the report does not place it near the light. No roster source for Canada beyond LighthouseFriends and the 1901 list (USLHS covers the US only). Record photo (Wikimedia Commons) not checked.
